name: rm
porting_notes: Port of OpenBSD rm 1.45. Uses amiport fts shim for recursive directory traversal (-R/-r flags). The -P secure overwrite flag is accepted but disabled since AmigaOS has no fstatfs() or fsync(). Interactive prompts (-i flag) work via stdin. rm_strmode() generates Unix-style permission strings from AmigaOS protection bits. 17/18 FS-UAE tests pass; 1 failure involves the -P flag interaction which is intentionally a no-op.
known_limitations: -P (secure overwrite) disabled: accepted for compatibility but performs no data overwriting since AmigaOS has no fstatfs() or fsync(). Permission display approximate: Unix-style strings generated from AmigaOS protection bits. User/group names always show amiga/amiga since AmigaOS has no multi-user system.

rm - Remove directory entries

Original author: The Regents of the University of California
Ported by Duncan Bowring using amiport (AI-assisted porting toolkit).
Project: https://github.com/bdgscotland/amiport

Cross-compiled with m68k-amigaos-gcc for AmigaOS 3.x (68000+).
Tested in vamos emulator and FS-UAE.

Usage:
  rm [-dfiRrv] file ...

Options:
  -d      Attempt to remove directories as well as files
  -f      Force removal without prompting
  -i      Prompt before each removal
  -R/-r   Remove directories and their contents recursively
  -v      Verbose: print files as they are removed

Note: The -P (secure overwrite) flag is accepted but has no
effect on AmigaOS. AmigaOS has no multi-user security model
requiring data sanitization before deletion.

Includes full source code (original POSIX and ported Amiga versions)
and PORT.md documenting every transformation applied.
